settings.lede: Pantao opens once a year. A single edition, made in numbers small enough to know each piece by hand — then the doors close until the next.

settings.heading: On the fifth edition.
settings.body:
Each year we ask the same question, and the answer changes. This edition asks how a garment can hold up in the weather without showing it. How an interior surface can do the work of a coat without announcing itself. Twelve pieces follow, made in numbers that allow us to know each one.

Members will receive their pieces with a card noting which one it is, and where it was made. We hope you wear them gently and often.

settings.definition: From the Tagalog tao — a person, a people.
settings.body: We take the name as an instruction. Clothing cut for the body and the life around it — worn gently, worn often, made in numbers that let us answer for each one. Not for the few. For the people who wear it.

settings.story: Open-gauge merino, distressed by hand. The openwork is worked deliberately at the wrist and the throat, so a watch reads at the cuff and a chain sits clear at the collarbone. Made in a count we can name.
